scope: India domestic + India-origin international, retail published fares, 5 carriers
_README: EVERY rule in this file was extracted from a primary source: the carrier's own live page,
its mandatory-disclosure PDF, or a dated Internet Archive capture. The verbatim quote that
produced each rule is stored on the rule itself. Nothing here is invented.
date_basis is the most important field. STATED means the carrier itself declares the
effective date on the page. OBSERVED means we only know a capture existed on that date and
the true start of the rule is unknown - which caps confidence at LOW. Only SpiceJet and
Akasa self-document effective dates; the other three do not.
applicability_key records WHICH date the version boundary keys to. SpiceJet keys to BOOKING
date ('for bookings before/on-or-after'). Where unknown it is UNKNOWN, not assumed.

confidence_rules.STATED: MEDIUM — carrier declares its own effective date
confidence_rules.OBSERVED: LOW — capture date only; true rule start unknown
confidence_rules.note: No policy-snapshot rule may ever exceed MEDIUM. Only a filed fare rule (ATPCO Cat 33) or an authoritative servicing quote can reach HIGH, and none of these carriers file Cat 33 for the tickets in scope.

source.quote: INR 4999 or Base fare + fuel surcharge (Whichever is lower). Cancellation fee will depend upon the time of cancellation. / INR 3499 or Base fare + fuel surcharge (Whichever is lower). / INR 3000 or Base fare + fuel surcharge
source.content_verification: PARTIALLY VERIFIED: the figures 3000/3499/4999 are present, but the capture interleaves a day-denominated table ('0-3 Days', '4 Days and above') with an hour-denominated one ('3-24', '24-72 Hours left'), so the band-to-amount mapping cannot be settled from the text alone.

corroborating_evidence.note: Domestic cancellation table is identical to the 2026-08-22 capture, verified 2026-09-08. Intermediate captures (2025-12-06, 2026-01-28, 2026-07-14) carry the same fee set.

caveats: Page carries NO effective date. Band-to-amount mapping inferred from descending fee order against the 3/24/72h band structure documented on the sibling fees-and-charges page.
Same capture contains a stale banner ('Full flexibility ... until 7 March 2026', already past at capture date) - a data-quality signal that IndiGo page text lags its live rules.
Marked disputed 2026-09-08: the capture mixes day-based and hour-based band labels in the same block, so this encoding is one plausible reading rather than a settled one.
Observed window widened back to 2025-09-09 on 2026-09-08: the domestic cancellation table in the 2025-09-09 capture is identical to this one, and three intermediate captures show the same fees.

FARE-FAMILY DIMENSION UNRESOLVED: the page prints columns 'Lite Fare | Regular Fare | Flexi Plus Fare | Return Fare', so IndiGo's table is NOT family-agnostic as this rule's '*' encoding assumes. The flattened capture text does not let the column-to-band mapping be settled, which is why the rule stays disputed. Re-transcribing it from the rendered page is an open corpus task.

conflicts_with.detail: Two IndiGo pages disagree for the overlapping period: fees-and-charges.html (captured 2025-07-08) gives 3999/3999/4999 for 72h+/24-72h/3-24h, while cancellation.html gives 3000/3499/4999. Neither page states an effective date, so which governs a given ticket is not established.

structurally_unverified.reason: The source prints a fare-family x time-band grid — columns 'Lite Fare | Regular Fare | Flexi Plus Fare | Return Fare', each with its own band label — but this rule encodes the figures as three time bands for all fare families. The flattened capture text cannot settle the column-to-band mapping, and the corpus's own caveat records the mapping as inferred. A number derived from a misread grid is wrong even at LOW confidence, so the rule is withheld from resolution until it is re-transcribed from the rendered page.
structurally_unverified.task: Re-transcribe IndiGo's cancellation grid per fare family from the rendered capture.

source.quote: Cancellation Fees: Domestic: 0-24 (Hours) - INR 4999 or 100% of the airfare charge (whichever is lower) 24-72 (Hours) - INR 3999 or 100% of the airfare charge (whichever is lower) 72 Hours + - INR 3999 or 100% of the airfare charge (whichever is lower). 100% of airfare will be forfieted for any changes or cancellations made within two (2) hours prior to the scheduled time of flight departure. No-Show Penalty: 100% of the airfare will be forfieted. [Terms] effective for bookings made from 20th August 2025 onwards.
source.content_verification: VERIFIED: bands, cut-off, cap wording and the carrier-stated effective date were all read back from the preserved copy on 2026-09-08.

caveats: Corrected 2026-09-08 against the preserved copy. The earlier encoding was wrong in four ways: it stated an effective date of 2026-05-12 (the copy says 'effective for bookings made from 20th August 2025 onwards'), omitted the 0-24h band entirely, recorded the 24-72h fee as uncaptured when the copy states it, and used a 4h cut-off where the copy says two (2) hours.
Fee is 'INR X or 100% of the airfare charge (whichever is lower)', encoded as LESSER_OF with an AIRFARE_100PCT cap — a cheap ticket can never owe more than it cost.
The copy also states a no-show penalty of 100% of the airfare. Not encoded as a band: no-show is outside the passenger-initiated cancellation scope of this rule.

Condition A of the published table (nil cancellation fee within 24h of booking when departure is more than seven days away) is encoded as `free_look`.
